steps: Acute: NSAID (e.g. naproxen) or paracetamol; add an oral triptan (e.g. sumatriptan 50–100 mg) if no vascular contraindication.
Add an antiemetic (metoclopramide / prochlorperazine) for nausea.
Treat early; rest in a dark, quiet room.
Limit acute drugs to <10–15 days/month to avoid medication-overuse headache.
Prophylaxis if frequent/disabling: propranolol, amitriptyline, topiramate or candesartan.

confirm: Recurrent moderate–severe, often unilateral throbbing headache ± aura, photophobia, nausea with a normal exam (ICHD-3). Image only for red flags.
disposition: Outpatient; neurology referral if refractory or atypical.
